belongs_to: Distributive property: 'In the case of positive integers, we used a rectangular arrangement of objects ... green tokens for positive numbers and red tokens for negative numbers ... the overall arrangement represents 4 x (2 + (-3))' (the figure next to this paragraph; the following 'Try This' asks to show -4 x (2 + (-3)) visually)
description: A rectangular arrangement of tokens inside one large rounded rectangle with a thin light-grey outline. Inside it, side by side, two smaller rounded rectangles (thin light-grey outline). LEFT box: 8 GREEN round tokens, each with a black '+' sign, in 4 rows x 2 columns (count verified: 4 rows, 2 per row = 8). RIGHT box (wider than the left): 12 ORANGE-RED round tokens, each with a black minus sign '-', in 4 rows x 3 columns (count verified: 4 rows, 3 per row = 12). Curly braces with labels: one large brace ABOVE the whole large rectangle (opening downward, tip pointing up at the middle) labelled '4 × (2 + (–3))'; two braces BELOW, one under the left box labelled '4 × 2' and one under the right box labelled '4 × (–3)' (tips pointing down). Labels are plain upright text in dark grey/black. White page background in the book. So the picture shows 4 × (2 + (–3)) = 4 × 2 + 4 × (–3) with 8 positive and 12 negative tokens.

belongs_to: Puzzle Time 'Terhüchü' (text on p.22): 'The board has 16 squares and diagonals are marked as shown in the following figure ... each player has a set of 9 coins placed as shown'; Gameplay: 'The starting position of the game is as shown above'
description: The Terhüchü board at the starting position, black line drawing on a pale pinkish-grey rectangle. MAIN SQUARE: a 4 x 4 grid of squares (16 squares) = 5 x 5 = 25 intersections; call columns c1-c5 left to right and rows r1-r5 top to bottom. Lines: 5 horizontal and 5 vertical lines through the intersections; both full diagonals of the main square (r1c1-r5c5 and r1c5-r5c1); and the four slanted lines joining the midpoints of the sides to each other (r1c3-r3c1, r1c3-r3c5, r3c1-r5c3, r3c5-r5c3, a diamond), so every intersection on the main diagonals/diamond has diagonal lines through it. EIGHT TRIANGLES outside the main square (the 'triangular corners'): four corner triangles, each a right triangle with its right angle at a corner of the main square, legs lying along the extended sides of the square and the hypotenuse outside, with extra inner lines (a line from the square's corner to the hypotenuse and a short line parallel to the hypotenuse); and four triangles in the middle of each side: top triangle with its apex at r1c3, base along the top, bottom triangle with apex at r5c3, left triangle with apex at r3c1 and base vertical on the left, right triangle with apex at r3c5 and base vertical on the right; each has a centre line from the apex to the base and a cross line. COINS (9 + 9 = 18, counted): 9 CYAN (light blue) coins at the top: r1c1, r1c2, r1c3, r1c4, r1c5 (5 coins in the top row); r2c2, r2c3, r2c4 (3 coins); plus 1 cyan coin in the TOP triangle, on its right slanted side where the cross line meets it (to the right of the centre line). 9 RED coins at the bottom: r5c1, r5c2, r5c3, r5c4, r5c5 (5 coins in the bottom row); r4c2, r4c3, r4c4 (3 coins); plus 1 red coin in the BOTTOM triangle, on its left slanted side where the cross line meets it (to the left of the centre line). The two coin sets are drawn in clearly different colours (cyan vs red). Vacant intersections at the start: the whole middle row r3 (c1-c5), r2c1, r2c5, r4c1, r4c5, and all intersections inside the other triangles. The side triangles (left, right) hold no coins; the four corner triangles hold no coins.
unclear: Exact internal lines of the eight outer triangles (cross lines, small inner lines) are small and approximated from the picture; the apex/base positions and the two triangle coins are certain
Whether the main-square midpoint diamond lines are drawn in every quadrant exactly as described was checked on the picture but lines are thin
